newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian ski resort braces for glacier break-up.
newsitem.headline: Italian ski resort braces for glacier break-up.

text.p: Skiers and hoteliers waited anxiously on Thursday for a huge chunk of ice to fall off a glacier on the Mont Blanc massif in northwestern Italy, jeopardising a mountain hamlet.
The authorities have evacuated up to 10 people from the hamlet of Planpincieux, which is deemed at risk, closing two hotels, three restaurants and some ski hire shops.
The road to Val Ferret, the valley which an ensuing avalanche is expected to hit, has been closed and skiers barred from a cross-country piste.

Glacier experts say 10,000 to 20,000 cubic metres of ice are poised to drop off "the nose" of a hanging glacier 4,050 metres (13,500 feet) up in the Grandes Jorasses peaks close to Mont Blanc, Europe's highest mountain, and the Courmayeur ski region.
"Today or tomorrow, in a few minutes or a few days, it's ready to come down," said Courmayeur mayor Ferdinando Derriard at his offices in the centre of the popular resort.

Experts who have monitored the ice movement over the last year calculate that a block 70 metres (230 feet) high, 100 metres (330 feet) across and two or three metres (seven to 10 feet) deep is about to fall off.

The glacier is 12 km (7.5 miles) from Courmayeur and its downhill pistes, which are in a different area of the valley. "There is no danger for the inhabitants, the houses, the tourists or the ski slopes," Derriard said.

But the impact of the falling ice was hard to predict. "The problem isn't the ice, it's the snow on the slopes below the ice. When there is lots of snow, like now, it can propel a lot of snow down into the valley," he said.

This is the second natural phenomenon to upset the ski season at Courmayeur. A rock slide in another part of the valley killed a skier last Saturday and rescuers are still searching for a second man they think was buried under the rocks.
Deputy Mayor Serafino Cosson said the resort had suffered from cancellations since, although he said it was unclear if fear of avalanches or bad weather was deterring holidaymakers.

Northern Italy has had heavy snowfalls this season and in addition the movement of a huge snow deposit before an avalanche displaces air and can create a powerful wind which flattens trees and damages buildings.
"Sometimes there is more danger from the air blast than there is from the snow which comes down afterwards," Derriard said.
An avalanche committee monitors ice temperature and humidity using computer equipment but it has been unable to get a closer look at the glacier for several days because of low-lying cloud.
Floriano Tarditi, 57, of the Chalet Proment Restaurant in Planpincieux, has been staying in Courmayeur since he was evacuated on Monday.

He said he had not felt afraid at being at the foot of the glacier and was more concerned about the loss of trade. "It's a situation which is damaging for us," he said. "We've been closed since Monday and you can lose a lot of work."
